title: The fall of Ernst Udet
pull: The ace who could not build an air force

facts.text: Ernst Udet, born in Frankfurt on 26 April 1896, shot down 62 enemy aircraft in World War I, more than any other German ace who survived the war.
Between the wars he was a famous stunt pilot and flew in mountain films with Leni Riefenstahl.
He joined the Nazi Party in 1933 after Hermann Goring promised to buy him two American Curtiss Hawk II biplanes. He became a champion of the dive bomber, such as the Ju 87 Stuka.
In 1936 he took over the technical office of the Reich Air Ministry, and on 1 February 1939 he became Generalluftzeugmeister, in charge of all aircraft production and supply for the Luftwaffe.
He was a poor administrator. He filled his staff with old flying friends and insisted on dive bombing ability even for aircraft not suited to it, slowing new designs.
After the invasion of the Soviet Union in 1941, the Luftwaffe's needs outran German production. Goring widened the power of Field Marshal Erhard Milch, who in effect became Udet's boss.
At a meeting on 12 November 1941, Messerschmitt officials produced documents showing falsified figures and altered orders. Five days later, on 17 November, Udet shot himself in his Berlin apartment.
He left words in red blaming Goring, whom he called the Iron One. The exact wording differs between accounts.
The regime hid the suicide. It announced that Udet had died testing a new weapon and gave him a state funeral attended by Hitler and Goring.
Milch took over his post and halted production of failed designs such as the Messerschmitt Me 210 and Heinkel He 177, sending them back for more development.

Ernst Udet, smiling, in the cockpit of a Fokker D.VIII (the card calls it his 'Baby Fokker', Fokker D8), Iron Cross marking on the fuselage. NARA 111-SC-159753 (naId 215877682), use Unrestricted, US government work, public domain. Cropped from the mount card scan (8306 px) to the print, 1920 x 1513. Taken 22 years before his death; the caption must say 1919. The young smiling ace against the story of his end works as contrast, not admiration. Frame on his face, upper center.

declassified.fact: Udet's funeral claimed another flier. Werner Molders, the Luftwaffe's leading fighter ace, was killed in a plane crash at Breslau while flying to Berlin for the funeral. Udet was buried in the Invalidenfriedhof in Berlin, beside Manfred von Richthofen, his old commander.

body:
Germany's most famous living fighter ace was put in charge of building the Luftwaffe's planes. He was not suited to the job.

17 November 1941. Ernst Udet shot himself in his Berlin apartment. He had downed 62 aircraft in World War I, more than any German ace who survived it, then became a famous stunt pilot.

From 1939 he ran all Luftwaffe aircraft production. He staffed his office with old flying friends and insisted on dive bombing even for designs unsuited to it, which slowed new planes. When the war in the East outran production, Field Marshal Erhard Milch was in effect placed over him, and a meeting on 12 November exposed falsified figures.

The regime said he had died testing a new weapon and gave him a state funeral. He had left words in red blaming Goring.

17 November 1941. Ernst Udet, a 62 victory ace of World War I, shot himself in Berlin after his failures in aircraft production came to light. The regime claimed he died testing a new weapon.
